scope: The value of information: Blackwell's theorem in both directions for finite states, signals and actions — garbling never raises the value of an experiment in any decision problem, the sublinear (mean-preserving spread) form, nonnegative value of information and the perfect-information bound; and conversely, an experiment at least as valuable in every decision problem garbles to the other, by separating hyperplanes, so with a full-support prior the two orders coincide; binary signals ordered by accuracy, with the value of guessing the state equal to the accuracy.
